display.purpose: The hero headline, once per site. Its second line is the accent phrase.

h1.purpose: The heading on each inner route.

h2.purpose: Section headings on the home page.

h3.purpose: Closing-panel headings and tool category headings.

card-title.purpose: Project names, role names, tool names inside a ruled cell.

body.purpose: Page leads, held to a max-w-2xl measure.

mono.purpose: Versions, stacks, repository paths, skills. Code and measurement only, never a technical costume.

label.purpose: Footer column headings only. Never an eyebrow above a heading.

motion.name: state-150
motion.purpose: Every colour state change on the site: link hover, cell hover, nav hover, icon tint. One duration, no exceptions.

motion.name: nudge-150
motion.purpose: The trailing arrow on a 'view all' link shifts on hover. The only transform in the system.

components.name: Brand Button
components.description: The single primary action per view. Always the outward path to GitHub.

components.name: Outline Button
components.description: Every secondary action. Hairline border, no fill.

components.name: Ruled Grid
components.description: The signature container. Cells share exact 1px rules formed by a grid gap over a rule-coloured parent, so a list reads as one table rather than a scatter of cards.
components.html: Placeholder Project OneReplace with a real project. This entry stands in to show a project carrying a full description.TypeScript  SvelteKitPlaceholder Project TwoA second entry, here to show how the shared hairline reads between two cells.Rust  WebAssembly
components.css: .ds-ruled { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr; background: var(--bg, #ffffff); border: 1px solid var(--line, #e4e4e7); border-radius: var(--radius, 4px); overflow: hidden; } .ds-ruled-cell { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 12px; padding: 20px; background: var(--bg, #ffffff); box-shadow: -1px 0 0 0 var(--line, #e4e4e7), 0 -1px 0 0 var(--line, #e4e4e7); text-decoration: none; font-family: 'Geist Variable', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; transition: background-color 150ms linear; } .ds-ruled-cell:hover { background: var(--surface-2, #f4f4f5); } .ds-ruled-cell:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--brand, #0891b2); outline-offset: -2px; } .ds-ruled-title { font-size: 0.9375rem; font-weight: 500; color: var(--fg, #09090b); } .ds-ruled-body { font-size: 0.875rem; line-height: 1.65; color: var(--fg-muted, #52525b); } .ds-ruled-meta { font-family: 'Geist Mono Variable', ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: 0.75rem; color: var(--fg-subtle, #71717a); }

components.name: Status Dot
components.description: Project state. A 6px dot plus its word, never a filled chip or tinted row, so meaning never rests on colour alone.
components.html: ActivePausedShipped
components.css: .ds-status { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; margin-right: 16px; font-family: 'Geist Variable', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.75rem; color: var(--fg-muted, #52525b); } .ds-status-dot { width: 6px; height: 6px; border-radius: 999px; flex-shrink: 0; } .ds-status-active { background: var(--ok, #15803d); } .ds-status-paused { background: var(--warn, #b45309); } .ds-status-shipped { background: var(--info, #1d4ed8); }

components.name: Placeholder Tag
components.description: Marks content standing in for something real. Dashed on purpose: the outline of something missing should not look like a finished chip.
components.css: .ds-placeholder { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; padding: 2px 6px; border: 1px dashed var(--line-strong, #d4d4d8); border-radius: 2px; font-family: 'Geist Variable', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.6875rem; font-weight: 500; line-height: 1; letter-spacing: 0.05em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--fg-subtle, #71717a); }

components.name: Panel
components.description: The closing anchor on every page: a one-step surface with a heading, a sentence and one action. The only container style besides the ruled grid.
components.html:

components.css: .ds-panel { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 8px; padding: 24px; background: var(--surface, #fafafa); border: 1px solid var(--line, #e4e4e7); border-radius: var(--radius, 4px); font-family: 'Geist Variable', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-panel-title { margin: 0; font-size: 1.125rem; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: -0.02em; color: var(--fg, #09090b); } .ds-panel-body { margin: 0; max-width: 42rem; font-size: 0.875rem; line-height: 1.65; color: var(--fg-muted, #52525b); }

components.description: A file path or dependency name inside prose. Mono is reserved for exactly this kind of literal.
components.css: .ds-code-line { margin: 0; font-family: 'Geist Variable', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.875rem; line-height: 1.65; color: var(--fg-muted, #52525b); } .ds-code { padding: 2px 6px; background: var(--surface-2, #f4f4f5); border-radius: 2px; font-family: 'Geist Mono Variable', ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: 0.75rem; color: var(--fg, #09090b); }

narrative.overview:
This is the category standard executed at full fidelity rather than treated as a fallback. It holds the finish level of Linear and Vercel, with the hero structure of vite.dev. It deliberately replaces an earlier skeuomorphic machine-shop world (enamel signs, manila job tickets, pegboard, hazard stripes) that put costume between the visitor and the code.

The governing rule is that nothing is decorated that is not also structural. Borders divide, they do not ornament. There are no textures, no gradient fields, no drop shadows on content, and no card scatter. The page is a quiet grey scale with hairline rules doing all the dividing; the only saturated colour in the building is the logo's cyan, and it is spent in four places and no others.
keyCharacteristics: Neutral ground, one accent. Restrained colour strategy throughout.
Hairline rules, not gaps: lists read as one ruled table, never a scatter of cards.
Squared corners: 4px by default, nothing above 8px except the scrollbar thumb.
Status is a dot and a word, never a coloured surface.
Absence is marked, quietly: a dashed PLACEHOLDER tag, never a hazard stripe.

rules.name: The Four Roles Rule
rules.body: Brand cyan may appear as: a primary button fill, link text, the active nav underline, the focus ring. There is no fifth role. brand-bright is the same hue one step up, and its only job is the hero headline's accent phrase.

rules.name: The Two Cyans Rule
rules.body: brand is a fill value and brand-text is a text value, because the fill is too light to set copy in on a white ground. Setting body copy in brand on light mode is the failure this split exists to prevent.

rules.name: Status Never Fills
rules.body: A status is a dot plus its word. A coloured chip, badge background, or tinted row is out of system.

rules.name: The Tracking Floor
rules.body: Headings tighten as they grow, and never past -0.04em. Body copy is never tracked.

rules.name: No Eyebrows
rules.body: No kicker or label sits above a heading. The heading carries its own weight.

rules.name: The Short Row Rule
rules.body: A ruled grid must always close into a complete rectangle, via two mechanisms together. First, cells draw their own top and left rules as a box-shadow rather than the grid showing a rule-coloured parent through a 1px gap; under the gap approach a track with no cell in it renders as a solid block of rule colour. Second, because rules then only exist where cells exist, a short last row leaves them stopping in mid-air, so every multi-column ruled grid carries ruled-fill-2 or ruled-fill-3, matching its maximum column count, which widens the final cell to close the row. A multi-column ruled grid without its matching fill utility is a bug, not a style choice.

dos: Do divide with a 1px line and nothing else.
Do put lists in a ruled grid so they read as one table.
Do mark every placeholder visibly, and keep the real Tools data honest.
Do design both modes as first-class; neither is a filter over the other.
Do theme the browser surfaces: selection, caret, scrollbar, focus ring.
Do keep mono for code, versions, paths and data.
donts: Don't spend brand cyan outside its four roles.
Don't add a shadow to content. There is no elevation system here.
Don't exceed 8px radius on any container.
Don't fill a surface with a status colour, or tint a row by state.
Don't put a kicker or eyebrow above a heading.
Don't introduce a second container style. panel and ruled are the two, and they are enough.
Don't reintroduce texture, paper, enamel or any material metaphor. That world was deliberately replaced.
Don't add a glow, halo or drop-shadow to the logo mark. A zero-offset coloured glow is decoration, not depth.
Don't use a multi-column ruled grid without its matching ruled-fill-2 or ruled-fill-3 utility; the last row will leave rules stopping in mid-air whenever the item count does not divide evenly.
